source: National Archives Amendments 11–27 transcript, Amendment XI
review_notes: Codex reviewed the complete Eleventh Amendment. The prohibition covers suits in law and equity and the three stated plaintiff categories; “commenced or prosecuted” remains a disjunction within each condition. It does not claim that the judicial power never reaches other kinds of suits. These are Codex labels, not independent human labels.
text:
AMENDMENT XI

The Judicial power of the United States shall not be construed to extend to any suit in law or equity, commenced or prosecuted against one of the United States by Citizens of another State, or by Citizens or Subjects of any Foreign State.
